questions.text: (Select the incorrect answer among the propositions below) The difference between the Gross National Income and the Gross Domestic Income:

options.a: is partly explained by the primary incomes earned by the country's fiscal residents working abroad
options.b: is equivalent to the difference between the Gross National Product and the Gross Domestic Product
options.c: is partly explained by the depreciation of the country's stock of physical capital over the considered period
options.d: is non-existent in a closed economy

questions.text: An individual's disposable income is obtained by:

options.a: summing up an individual's primary and secondary incomes
options.b: correcting an individual's primary income for taxes
options.c: summing up an individual's primary income, secondary incomes and financial assets, before correcting for the personal income tax
options.d: adding benefits and retrieving direct taxes from an individual's primary income

questions.text: (Select the incorrect answer among the propositions below) The money multiplier:

options.a: depends on the share of money that agents want to hold in currency form
options.b: depends on the aggregate price level in the considered economy
options.c: depends on the money reserves held by commercial banks
options.d: depends on the share of money that agents want to hold on checkable deposits

questions.text: Inflation has spiked in the industrialised countries over the last two years, which led most Central Banks to raise their interest rates. According to our modelling of the monetary market, this increase in interest rates following an increase in the inflation rate will:

options.a: have an undetermined impact on the money demand, because several effects are impacting it in opposite directions
options.b: decrease the money demand, because of the variation in its opportunity cost
options.c: increase the money demand, because of the variation in its opportunity cost
options.d: increase the money demand, because of the increase in prices

options.a: insufficient labor supply and insufficient production capacities
options.b: insufficient labor supply and underemployed production capacities
options.c: insufficient labor demand and underemployed production capacities
options.d: insufficient labor demand and insufficient production capacities

questions.text: In the IS-LM model without expectations, a fiscal consolidation will, all other things being kept equal, lead to:

options.a: a stronger contraction of economic activity if it is carried out via a reduction of public expenditures than if it is carried out via an increase in the tax level
options.b: an identical contraction of economic activity, whether it is carried out via a reduction of public expenditures or via an increase in the tax level
options.c: a stronger contraction of economic activity if it is carried out via an increase in the tax level than if it is carried out via a reduction of public expenditures
options.d: none of the above answers are correct, since the model does not make it possible to compare the multiplying effect of public expenditures and of taxes

questions.text: In IS-LM in a closed economy, the IS relationship guarantees that the public deficit:

options.b: is equal to private savings minus private investments
options.c: is equal to private savings minus private and public investments
options.d: is equal to private savings plus private investments

questions.text: In the WS-PS model, it is assumed that:

options.a: workers and employers reason in nominal terms
options.b: workers reason in real terms and employers reason in nominal terms
options.c: workers and employers reason in real terms
options.d: workers reason in nominal terms and employers reason in real terms

questions.text: Economic analysts agree that in most developed economies, the number of job vacancies is currently being equal to (or even higher than) the number of unemployed workers. According to the modelling of the labor market we have provided in our lectures, this should lead to:

options.b: An increase in investments aiming at replacing the labor factor by machines
options.c: An increase in public expenditures, since those include training programs for unemployed workers
options.d: Both an increase in public expenditures and in replacement investments

questions.text: In the AS-AD model and starting from the medium-run equilibrium, would a government finding the aggregate price level too high consider raising taxes?

options.a: No, because in the medium-run, raising taxes leads to a higher price level
options.b: Yes, because in the medium-run, raising taxes leads to a lower price level while leaving the economic activity unchanged
options.c: Yes, because in the medium-run, raising taxes leads to a higher level of economic activity while leaving the price level unchanged
options.d: No, because in the medium-run, raising taxes leads to a lower economic activity level

questions.text: Consider a macroeconomic policy raising the level of social benefits for certain categories of the population, and a macroeconomic policy promoting competition:

options.a: the two policies both aim at stimulating aggregate demand
options.b: the first one aims at stimulating aggregate demand, and the second aims at stimulating aggregate supply
options.c: the first one aims at stimulating aggregate supply, and the second aims at stimulating aggregate demand
options.d: the two policies both aim at stimulating aggregate supply

questions.text: The unemployment rate is currently at a relatively low level in industrialised countries. According to the original Phillips curve, should such a situation lead to higher inflation levels?

options.a: No, because the unemployment rate has no effect on inflation
options.b: No, because it is the variation of the unemployment rate that matters
options.d: No, because the methodological flaws in the measurement of the unemployment rate make it loose its relevance when trying to predict price variations

questions.text: For a Central Bank, the "zero floor constraint":

options.a: limits the possibility to sustain economic activity through a monetary expansion when expected inflation levels are low
options.b: limits the possibility to sustain economic activity through a fiscal expansion when markets are starting to consider the possibility of a sovereign default
options.c: limits the possibility to fight inflation via a monetary contraction
options.d: none of the above answers are correct

questions.text: In the IS-LM model, taking expectations of agents relative to the future output and tax levels into account modifies:

options.a: the LM curve, but not the IS curve
options.b: the IS curve, but not the LM curve
options.c: both the IS curve and the LM curve
options.d: the IS curve, and the LM curve in the case of an increasing LM curve

questions.text: Consider an economy initially at the medium-run equilibrium and facing a contraction in economic activity, in which the government is considering sustaining economy activity via a fiscal policy. According to the IS-LM framework with expectations, a strategy that could boost the impact of such a stimulus policy is to:

options.a: sustain private consumption rather than investment
options.b: lower taxes rather than increase benefits
options.d: combine it with a credible restrictive monetary policy
